chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) forbade four teknonyms: Abu Isa, and Abu al-Hakam, and Abu Malik, and Abu al-Qasim when the name is Muhammad.
ai.seo_question: Which four kunyas are forbidden for someone named Muhammad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet's prohibition of four specific kunyas for those named Muhammad, with 'Abu al-Qasim' being the most significant as it is the kuny of the Prophet himself, reserved to avoid confusion or presumption of equality. The exclusion of 'Abu Isa' and 'Abu al-Hakam' reflects the desire to distinguish the bearer from the Prophet or to avoid titles associated with specific divine attributes or other prophets. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on preserving the unique status of the Prophet and his family through precise nomenclature.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
that the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> forbid from four teknonyms – from Abu Isa, and from Abu Al-Hakam, and from Abu Maalik, and from Abu Al-Qasim when the name was Muhammad’.
en.sarwar: 15. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, prohibited four Kunyah like abu ‘Isa, abu al-Hakam, abu Malik, abu al-Qasim if the name is Muhammad.’”
